plan: My private value is $28. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is often to bid close to my true value. Since the values are randomly drawn, I can't predict other bidders' values. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning while still maintaining potential profit. A bid around $30-$35 seems strategic - high enough to likely win, but not so high that I risk losing money if I win.

My private value is $23. In a first-round single auction, optimal strategy is to bid strategically near my value. Since the prize is randomly valued between $0-$49, I'll aim to bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances. A bid around $25-$26 gives me a buffer to potentially win while minimizing overpayment risk. I want to win, but not pay more than the item's worth to me.

With a private value of $36, I want to maximize potential profit. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value but not exactly at it. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances while protecting downside. A bid around $38-$40 seems strategic - high enough to likely win, but not so high that I risk significant loss if I win. I'll aim to capture most of my value's surplus.
